reviews.title: Became too profit driven, deleting the app
reviews.text:
Once an app gets too big, the app starts to lose focus of the app’s main purpose. That’s what happened to Forest. 

It used to be so straight forward, which is just to track your study time and you get a digital tree in your forest for studying. Now, it’s all about trying to make you buy coins, pop ups after pop ups, and trying to get you to get this type of tree and plant. It’s so silly to me. Do they not know the demographics of their users? 

Are people really paying for “coins”? And for what? JUST focus on studying and passing your class/exams. 

The last straw for me was the app removing the total focus  time of the day on the main screen. what?? That’s literally the whole point of a study app…. To track your total time spent studying. 

I know they see their growing user base and now all they think about is how to extract money from each of them. It’s literally just a study app.. what kind of big money do y’all really think you will eventually make? 

Farewell. I’ll be using another study app from now on.

reviews.title: Too much AI, which is a shame.
reviews.text: I bought forest a while ago and it really improved my study sessions. It’s genuinely an amazing app and I love that you can buy the customizations for free if you just focus enough and grow enough trees. I also think the in-game coins to real life trees system is amazing! If only you didn’t immediately kill those trees by promoting the use of AI. I stopped using the app a few years ago and picked it back up for college, and everything changed. The user interface is TERRIBLE. It’s slow when trying to go anywhere but the main planting menu. And when you are done with a session, you click like 5 times on a button that says go home. I clicked “Go home” already, let me go. Other people have tried emailing support with complaints about ads (since I was an early supporter, I get an ad free experience) and they got a fully generative AI response which included the AI thinking process, of which included the AI not furthering the request for a refund because the user said they “wished” they could request a refund instead of saying “I would like to request a refund.” It’s insane to me that a company who promotes trees and understands that people do, in fact, like trees, doesn’t understand that using AI to generate and manage your entire app is scummy. This company should be ashamed.

reviews.title: Love with caveats
reviews.text: I use this app every day. I mostly use it for writing my novel because it creates structure and prevents me from drifting off into ADHD land. But when I’m in the flow of writing, I don’t want to stop mid-thought. The recent update made it impossible to push a button and restart the timer. It takes me three clicks to get back to the screen where I can restart it. It sounds like a small thing, but it shifts my thinking to the app rather than my writing. Please please please restore the ability to restart the timer with one click!

reviews.title: It’s nice!
reviews.text:
So let me start with, I really like this app. It’s improved a lot! I love how the tree’s is growth process is no longer inside a circle. I also really like how you can plant real trees! I bought this app about 2-4 years ago, so not much ago, but I am a pro user. I was a bit disappointed because it went free, but most of all, it started having a subscription. Then, I quit the app. This year, about a week or two ago I finally downloaded it again. I’m still really disappointed that there’s a subscription even for people who payed for it first, but it’s still a nice app. Also, I couldn’t find the actual prices of the subscription in the app. Just a trial. I would like to at least know how much it costs before I have a trial! Overall, I recommend this. There have been ways it’s been disappointing but I get it, and this app has really improved in the time I left it. It’s clean, and kids and teens and adults can use it. (I do have ad-blocker though, so I’m not sure if this app has ads, and if appropriate, but the app itself is clean!) Thanks for reading my long review!
EDIT: I put my tree and then worked in Quizlet. I went back to the app to check on it. The screen was white, so I just got out and in, then it said I killed my tree, and it died. I didn’t do anything, though? That was 50 minutes lost. :(

reviews.title: Retro User
reviews.text:
I first downloaded this app about 6 years ago and used it with a friend. We both loved it; it was a simple way to keep us both off our phones and on task. Each of us even bought a subscription. 

These past few months, the UI updates and AI integration have made this app so, so clunky. It breaks my heart to say that it's an eyesore now. The designs feel so much less simple and human-made. Clicking through a series of prompts makes the planting feature less efficient to use. 

Please, please offer some settings to help us go back to the way things were. Cut the AI garbage and cumbersome UI. For an app that espouses the value of getting off screen and going out into the world to do good (planting trees irl, getting your work done and be a functioning person), the AI integration is such a big disappointment. 

I've been actively searching for better apps to use. Please Forest, listen to those of us posting here and online.

reviews.title: Favorite Studying Tool
reviews.text: If you’re someone who loves to game-ify the mundane, this app should be right up your alley. I didn’t think this would be my holy grail study tool, but that’s what it’s become. Being able to look back and see all the progress I’ve made studying for my Associates and now my Bachelors is so reaffirming and inspiring. I really love the newer “stopwatch” feature, as instead of having the pressure of meeting a certain time, I’m able to just go with the incentive that if I hit that 2-hour make, the tree will surely come into full bloom. I’d recommend this app to anyone who wants a gentle nudge away from their phone for any reason, and I’m seriously considering upgrading to Premium because I just love the app, and they have an incredible mission behind them (which is what drew me in to begin with)!

reviews.title: Stop asking for money
reviews.text:
Stop monetizing everything. Stop pushing the subscription onto everyone. I already paid you, I’m not giving you more. And a lot of users are probably students who should be pressured into paying for features that should be free. Trend analysis as tags aren’t exactly special features that should be behind a paywall. 

It’s so obvious that you only care for the people who pay the subscription. Everything good goes to them. They get bonus daily tasks for gems. They get new trees. I have thousands of coins and absolutely nothing to spend them on because you’re only focusing on things for your subscription. And that’s after the shop got “fixed.” Which it didn’t, not really. You got rid of bundles, which I was saving for since they were a little discounted. You have to hope you’re lucky and get a gem tree that you want when you finally saved enough. We wanted more trees, not whatever this is. 

Just stop. You’ve pushed so many people away from your app because you keep ruining it. You made it take so long just to get to the Home Screen after a session. My app glitched on me today and the alert that the session stopped and rewards came an hour after I stopped it. You made an entire event on a feature that so many people couldn’t find at first since finding it isn’t intuitive. 

Please, for the love of God, stop making this app worse. Stop asking for money when people have already paid.

reviews.title: New Update Very Frustrating
reviews.text:
I’ve used and enjoyed this app for years, but this new update made sometime in September or October of 2026 has significantly reduced my satisfaction and compelled me to write this review. 

In some apparent effort to make the app something more profitable or inspiring more engagement, they have added all sorts of “events” and continued to focus on the coin shop. Worst of all, though, is they changed the UI so now I have to tap roughly 4 times to exit a timer I just set, when it used to be once. The app also no longer displays my total focus time for the day without having to tap 3-4 times to go see it on a separate screen. Why? They’ve also made many overtures to get me to “relax” as if this is a meditation app or something.

I bought this years ago just to time my focus and track my progress, as well as have a motivator in the form of the tree. Please just keep this simple or give me the option to strip away the excessive features that don’t serve that purpose and make this app more convoluted. I will have to move to a different method in the future, otherwise, and that saddens me since I’ve used this for 5+ years without issue until now.

reviews.title: UI has made me unfortunately delete the app
reviews.text: I’ve been using Forest for three years now, enjoyed it up until this recent update which has made using the app increasingly frustrating and it feels like a shell of its former self. Why remove the time ring? Why add three menus after planting a tree? Why implement all these clunky animations? reviews.title: Downhill Slide
reviews.text: I’ve used this app since 2016 and have been a huge advocate for it since early days. While I can’t think of any period of time in the past decade where the Forest app has maintained excellent stability free of glitches, the overall usefulness of the app has allowed me to look past that. In the past 12-18 months, things have been going downhill. The devs keep pushing out excessive updates that prioritize gamification in the app and focus on money-making capacity of the app. All the while, stability in the app for users like myself and my friends has decreased and glitches have increased to the point of a non-functional app. Sharing session links, planting together, and Deep Focus mode are all useless now with the rollout of a new UI and the retirement of “classic” mode. It’s a real shame. I’ve accumulated over 275 days of planting time in this app, the majority of which were logged in Plant Together mode with friends. I’ll be sad to leave the app and my land of virtual trees behind, but it may be the natural course of things if the devs continue to ignore prioritization of the function and stability of the Forest app.

reviews.title: I love this app, but…
reviews.text:
I really love this app. I’ve been using it for years and have found it very helpful to focus and track my writing time. However, since the introduction of focus challenge I have been annoyed by the implementation. My biggest issue is the fact that I have to reset my focus timer each time I want to “plant a tree” for the challenge. If I do 2 hours in the app, it says I planted 4 trees in my forest but only one tree for the daily challenge. If the daily challenge says “plant any tree 4 times” I have to start and stop my focus timer four times (once every 30 minutes) in order for the trees to count. Why? The fact that I have to interrupt my focus time to stop and reset in order to achieve the daily challenge is ridiculous. It’s actually the opposite of focus, enough that I may have to switch to a different app because it is distracting me trying to keep my trees and focus time to match. 

Please fix this. Make it so that when I focus for a number of hours, the daily challenge counts my trees planted, not by the number of times I started focusing. It feels like a bug, but it’s been present since the focus challenge released. Thanks!

reviews.title: New look and streamlined-ness kind of terrible, otherwise love it
reviews.text:
Been using this app for years and love it. Don’t seem to have the glitches every other review talks about. But they keep changing the look of the app, and where buttons are, and what direction you need to scroll to pick a tree or a focus title you have, and they do this like every 2-3 months it seems. It makes it feel extremely inconsistent, and when I’ve finally gotten the muscle memory down for the app to feel streamlined and easy to use and find everything in, they suddenly change all of it again, and it becomes frustrating. Pick a look that works and stick with it. Why change the look if it’s not broken? This most recent look/button/scrolling update is so bad it makes me not want to use the app. Everything got enlarged so huge, text runs off the edge of the menu. Buttons are huge, yet for any function I need to go through hoops of multiple buttons or menus, when before it was just one button or everything in one menu. I need to click stop, then collect reward, when before it just collected reward automatically no extra button press needed. Now I need to pick a focus and a tree in two separate menus, tap to enter tree select menu, tap to exit, tap to enter focus title menu, tap to exit. Before these things were in the same menu. What was two buttons to enter and then exit menu, is now 4, since it’s been split into two menus. The way to scroll through trees vertically instead of horizontally feels wrong…who thinks of trees as being stacked on top of each other? No one. It feels kind of unintuitive and unnatural. And now because text is huge, scrolling vertically to pick a focus title out of many that I have is just a hassle and very ugly looking. Maybe this works for people used to reading text vertically, and could be used in those regions, or an option to switch between one or the other for those who prefer that direction of reading, but scrolling vertically through theses feels unnatural to me as well. When reading my eyes want to move left to right, the way it was horizontally scrolling before. But now my brain has to stop and start and stop and start as it jumps up and down the vertical list. 
The extra buttons and menus, and the new scrolling format makes using the app take twice as much time as it did before, which is taking away from the time people want to be focusing on whatever they’re getting set up to focus on. It just feels like twice as much work to use the app now. And everything in the app seems extra large now, like I accidentally bought an extra large print book. I’m not sure who they were making this update for, but it feels like it is not for students or young adults anymore.

reviews.title: Recommended by OT but not quite doing the job.
reviews.text:
I have AUDHD with some OCD, anxiety and exhaustion. I am dealing with physical disability as well from nervous system and autoimmune issues. I’m in occupational therapy for speech, physical rehab, and soon will be adding visual OT. My speech therapist thinks that the root of a lot of my problems is actually exhaustion from excessive screen time. My screen time has become an escape hatch from my preexisting issues, but it worsens them so it’s an endless feedback loop. We are using this app to try stepping down from my usage of social media in particular. 


Most of us have multiple devices. I have an iPad, MacBook, iPhone and Apple Watch and the app doesn’t automatically sync across these devices. It doesn’t automatically lock down all my devices, I have to grow a tree separately on each even after syncing them. 

It doesn’t reliably block access to apps when in focus mode. It says I’m in focus right now and I can access all my apps without killing my tree. 

I don’t like the stats board. I have premium and it is showing me whatever I’ve tagged my usage as, instead of using existing Apple analytics to populate that chart. Rocket money and Mint seem to be able to create good pie charts and graphs based off access to account info, so wondering why this isn’t the same. 

I find the current description key for the charts comparing one day against another a bit vague. More concise wording is needed to provide a key to understanding that one. Is this even a helpful metric? Why not something more simple and engaging like “wow, you did it! Your break from screens lasted 20% longer than yesterday, with a total of 4.5 hours!” The way it’s set up now is very flat and boring and tbh hard to tell if it’s a positive or negative comparison. 

The daily challenge always has one goal I can’t meet without cashing in all my coins on a plant I don’t have to unlock it. Not a fan of that as a premium user. 

I did like being able to set focus to run from a set time in morning to a set time in evening. I didn’t like that it doesn’t automatically remember this setting and do it every day Monday through Friday (or whatever you prefer). It did it well for my first day, and then wasn’t in place the next morning. I really need the features to run for consecutive days in order for this to work. Relying on me to remember or have the willpower to do this every day in the beginning is not helpful. I have adhd, this is not accounting for how our disability shows up. We are more prone to addiction to screens, and have more difficulty creating new habits, especially when the new habit is in conflict with an established maladaptive ritual. A setting where I can explain what level assistance I need, and then consent to a time frame or schedule for the week/month would work better than what it’s doing now. 


I’d love to see a journal of symptoms and encouragement/coping strategies  included in the app. Other addiction apps provide structured support for the hard parts of cycle breaking. Since I’m doing this on the recommendation of a doctor, would be cool to be able to log symptoms and share that kind of chart with them over time. To view my progress that way. 
For example, I experienced a lot of anxiety and agitation my first day. I had observations about my energy levels, and would like to have stored what I did with my time instead on the app for a productivity chart or something. I also experienced insomnia my first night, and would have benefitted from charting that, sleep as a metric is useful, and possibly links to resources to help fall asleep. 


I hate the “take a break” options. The breathing animation and “peaceful sounds” are awful. They’re loud and distracting, and without sound pretty useless. The breathing is way too fast for calming down. 

And last, I much prefer setting up the app to block my access to specific things for a set time period, vs checking it every 20 minutes or so to get a tree. Why cant we still get trees and coins for the time we are in deep focus for hours? I get ONE tree no matter how long the break is. Repeatedly checking the app is defeating the purpose of staying off the device. Picking it up to do that makes me want to check social media. I’m trying to wean off the default of looking at my phone during my more functional hours when I should be doing IRL things.

reviews.title: Shout out to the Forest team for caring about user satisfaction! 💯
reviews.text:
I’m really impressed by how quickly the team addressed the issues I mentioned in a previous review (they were fixed within hours).

In that review, I also suggested bringing back more flexibility with pauses, since some users need short breaks when they notice their attention starting to fade. Being able to pause when needed makes it easier to stay focused during longer sessions and helps Forest better support users who have difficulty concentrating for extended periods.

The app is great as it is, in my opinion, but to better accommodate different users’ needs and study styles without making it too tempting to pause constantly, one suggestion would be to add a setting that lets users toggle between one pause per session and unlimited pauses. Giving users the option to choose their preferred pause setting would make Forest more flexible and supportive for different attention spans and routines.

Overall, I really enjoy Forest and value that the developers listen to user feedback. Thank you for continuing to improve Forest and for creating a functional platform that helps us stay focused and reach our goals.
